blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — cyclophosphamide urotoxicity prevention and monitoring
stem: A client is receiving IV cyclophosphamide. Which nursing action best addresses an important urinary-tract toxicity of this medication?

options.A: Provide prescribed hydration, promote frequent bladder emptying when appropriate, and monitor urine for hematuria because cyclophosphamide can cause serious bladder toxicity.
options.B: Restrict fluid intake around treatment because hydration increases bladder exposure to toxic cyclophosphamide metabolites and raises hemorrhagic-cystitis risk.
options.C: Treat new hematuria as unrelated to cyclophosphamide because urinary-tract injury is not a recognized toxicity and does not require treatment reassessment.
options.D: Limit monitoring to cardiac function because bladder and renal surveillance are not relevant to cyclophosphamide-associated adverse effects.

rationale: Current cyclophosphamide labeling reports hemorrhagic cystitis, hematuria, and other urotoxicity. Urinary sediment should be checked for erythrocytes and signs of urotoxicity/nephrotoxicity. Aggressive hydration with forced diuresis and frequent bladder emptying can reduce bladder toxicity. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Prevent and detect cyclophosphamide-associated hemorrhagic cystitis through hydration, bladder emptying, and hematuria monitoring.
source_locator: §5.2 Urinary Tract and Renal Toxicity: hemorrhagic cystitis and hematuria reported; check urinary sediment for erythrocytes; aggressive hydration with forced diuresis and frequent bladder emptying reduces bladder toxicity.
source_claim_supported: Cyclophosphamide urotoxicity is reduced by hydration/frequent bladder emptying and detected by urine monitoring for hematuria/erythrocytes.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: implement protective measures, monitor urinary toxicity, and recognize/report hematuria.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Removed absolute-word cues and balanced all options as complete urotoxicity-management statements.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches current cyclophosphamide labeling; no residual cue or second answer remains.
